claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand your situation with your child(ren).

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- Their exact age (or age range if you have more than one child)
- If you have multiple children, I can assess each one

This will help me guide you through the eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old. That's helpful to know.

Since Alex is 8 years old (under 16), let me move forward with the next check in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to ask you about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, the expectation is that they're not working. This is mainly a check that applies to older children, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8, so they're just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's what I expected. Alex is clearly not working, which is perfect for eligibility purposes.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about any benefits Alex might be receiving:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

Again, at age 8, this would be very unusual, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just 8, so nothing like that applies to them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's as expected for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship, or not?**

Since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I assume they're not in any apprenticeship, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - Alex is only 8 and in primary school. They're not in any apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important part of the eligibility criteria.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

Or if not, could you tell me more about your residency status? For example:
- Are you living abroad?
- Do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

This will help me understand which residency requirement applies to you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Leeds.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes things straightforward. You normally live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. This is about whether you have responsibility for the child's care and upkeep.

**How is your responsibility for Alex set up? Please tell me:**

- Do you live with Alex?
- Or are you contributing to Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, housing, pocket money)?
- Or are you paying maintenance under a court order or agreement?

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute to their upkeep. I help out with things like clothes and pocket money for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! So you're contributing to Alex's upkeep through clothes and pocket money. That's helpful to know.

Just to clarify for the assessment, could you tell me:

**Roughly how much do you contribute per week or per month to Alex's upkeep?**

This helps me confirm that your contributions are at least at the level of Child Benefit payments. I don't need an exact figure, but an approximate amount would help. (For reference, Child Benefit is currently £24.50 per week for the first child, though I can check the exact current rates if needed.)

This will help me verify that your level of contribution meets the criteria for responsibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's helpful. At £30 per week, your contributions clearly meet the threshold for Child Benefit (which is currently £24.50 per week for the first child). This satisfies the responsibility requirement.

Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question about other claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any dispute about who should be claiming?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (or anyone else) also claiming or planning to claim Child Benefit for Alex?
- If yes, have you agreed between yourselves who should claim?
- Or is there a disagreement about who should be the main claimant?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me wanting to claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - there's no other claimant, so there's no dispute. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's current living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living? Please tell me if any of these apply:**

- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is Alex in care (e.g., local authority care)?
- Is Alex fostered?
- Or is Alex living normally at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally - they're with their other parent, not in hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's straightforward. Alex is living normally. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the end of the assessment. I just need to check one final thing:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council not funding Alex's housing or upkeep?
- This would typically only apply if Alex was in some form of council-funded care arrangement

I assume this doesn't apply to your situation since Alex is living normally with their other parent, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex - they just live with their other parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I needed to know. Based on all the information you've provided, I can now give you the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit** ✓

### **Your Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**. Here's a summary of why:

✓ **Alex is a qualifying child** - aged 8 (under 16)  
✓ **You have responsibility for Alex** - you contribute £30 per week towards their upkeep (clothes, pocket money, etc.)  
✓ **You live in the UK** - you're based in Leeds  
✓ **No disqualifying factors** - Alex isn't working full-time, not receiving benefits, not in apprenticeship, not in care  
✓ **No other claimant** - no dispute over who should claim

---

### **What You Need to Do Next:**

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** - You can apply:
   - Online at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
   - Or by post using form CH2

2. **Prepare these documents:**
   - Proof of identity for yourself
   - Proof of identity for Alex
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important to know:**
   - If you or a partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may be liable for the High Income Child Benefit Charge (though you'll still be eligible to claim)
   - Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

---

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or need further assistance, feel free to ask!
